content.thinking:
I'm designing a kitsune fox standing in a rest pose facing forward, with nine fanned tails and spirit flames. I'm sizing it as a large fantasy fox—roughly 0.75m at the shoulder with tails extending about 1.1m upward in a fan shape.

I'm now building the skeleton: a hip root joint, then a spine chain curving from hips to chest using catmull points, followed by a neck chain running up to the head joint, being careful to use valid chain and joint APIs with proper parenting between segments.

For the jaw I'm adding a joint parented to the head with an absolute position and aim target, then planning a body sweep that threads through a path spanning tail, hips, spine, and neck bones to give the silhouette its volume.

For color I'm layering a cel-shaded fur edge paint in orange with a cream belly transition and ink outline. Then I'm planning the head construction with a skull sphere, snout sweep, extruded ears, decal eyes, and nose placed near the forward joint.

Working out skull and jaw placement with scaled spheres and tapered rod sweeps for upper and lower jaw, plus a small dark nose sphere, and I'm now adding spiky cheek fur tufts projecting outward and back from the sides.

For the ears, I'm defining a sharp-pointed extrusion outline and positioning it angled forward near the top of the skull, working through orientation vectors to keep the ear facing the right direction.

Now I'm adding an inner ear detail as a smaller pink extrusion layered just above the base ear shape, then moving on to placing eye decals using surface projection onto the skull.

Picking amber-gold iris tones for the kitsune eyes and sizing them proportionally, then building a skull coloration using a fur-edge cel shader that blends orange fur into a cream muzzle based on vertical position.

Now I'm setting up the four legs with IK chains -- front legs get a three-segment structure (shoulder, elbow, wrist) sized to span the distance from shoulder joint to foot target, with bend hints pulling the elbow backward and the wrist forward for a natural fox gait.

For the hind legs I'm using similar lengths with the knee bending forward and hock bending back, keeping the lower leg segment roughly vertical, and naming each chain's joints (shoulder/elbow/wrist/paw, hip/knee/hock/paw) with side suffixes, parenting the front legs to the chest joint in the spine.

I'm also figuring out the sweep radii tapering down each limb and deciding to paint the lower legs darker to form sock-like markings against the lit coat color.

For the paws, I'm shaping flattened spheres positioned at the chain's tip joint, and considering small cream-colored claw spikes before deciding whether they're worth the extra part count.

Now I'm designing the nine tails fanning out from the hip base, computing directional vectors with varying angle and elevation so the center tails sweep higher while outer ones spread wider, then building control points along each curve for an upward sweeping path.

Still working out tail curvature...

For thickness, I'm shaping a teardrop radius that bulges near the middle and tapers to a point at the tip, with the base attached to the hips. For color, I'm defining banded orange-to-cream gradient paint along the sweep of the tail.

I'm also adding glowing flame cards at each tail tip, using cross-oriented flame textures and attaching glow effects to those meshes.

I'm layering the flame colors as teardrop violet outside with cyan inner and white core. For extra atmosphere, I'm scattering 6-7 floating spirit orbs (hitodama) around the fox, each with a small glowing sphere core and upward-facing flame cards attached to the nearest joint, positioned loosely around head height.

I also want crimson kitsune face markings, so I'm placing a red decal on the forehead using a hit-based orientation—setting the decal direction mostly upward and slightly forward, with an up vector tilted to keep it roughly facing outward on the skull surface.

For the cheeks, I'll mirror two red swoosh decals on either side, angled outward from the face center. Then for the neck, I'm thinking ornate gold jewelry—a beaded necklace with tassels, a magatama pendant, and maybe a red ribbon accent to fit the high-fantasy anime look.

Now I need to figure out the neck geometry itself: whether to loop a cutting plane through the neck joint to define the collar region, keeping the body sweep ending at the chest and treating the neck as a separate swept section so the plane doesn't accidentally slice through the torso.

Still layering the bib colour logic...

For the overall palette I'm settling on golden-orange body fur with cream accents, vermilion markings, violet flame details, gold ornaments, and dark socks and ear backs for a celestial kitsune look. For the collar I'm adding a shimenawa-style red rope swept along the loop, with gold beads spaced along it.

Placing the gold pendant...

Adding tassel cards hanging from the pendant and considering gold rings around the tail bases, sweeping frames along each tail for placement.

I'll pass the chain point's frame directly for orientation so the gold torus follows the tail's tangent correctly. For extra gold details I'm considering small ear rings and a tiny forehead gem near the skull's top-front position, though I may keep these minimal to avoid overcomplicating the design.

Now I'm computing the exact forehead point using the skull's radii and elevation angle, then placing a small violet-glowing octahedron gem there alongside a smaller red crescent decal positioned slightly lower so they don't overlap. I'm also starting to plan the nine tails, making sure their base positions avoid colliding with the hind legs and body.

For the tail fluff, I'm scattering orange fur-tuft wisp cards across each tail's surface using a sweep, tinting the greyscale texture orange to keep it lightweight in triangle count while considering whether to apply flat or shaded paint.

For color, I'm using a distance-based paint function that checks each point's proximity to the tail tip, coloring it cream near the tip and orange elsewhere, then reusing that same paint logic for both the sweep surface and the fluff cards so the blend stays consistent without needing extra gradient bands.

Now I'm working on the flow direction for the tail wisp cards, projecting an upward vector onto the hit surface so wisps lean along the tail toward the tip instead of drooping backward, pairing that with a cross-facing setting so the cards stay visible from more angles.

For body fur, I'm adding cream-colored chest fluff cards scattered on the front neck region using a normal-based filter, plus thin whisker rods extending from the muzzle in pairs on each side.

Now I'm working out the mouth details: small white fang cones on the upper jaw pointing downward, skipping the tongue and mouth line decal. I'm positioning the jaw and snout as separate rod bones with specific radii and endpoints, checking how the gap between upper and lower parts should align at the joint.

Checking that the jaw overlap stays closed with slight tolerance given the radii and tip positions, then confirming the skull sphere size and adding a small nose sphere. Now I'm setting up cheek ruff spikes radiating outward from the jaw area, planning three spikes per side with varied directions using mirrored x-coordinates.

Working out the ear placement and orientation vectors, checking the cross product to confirm the ear's local axes face the right way when mirrored to the opposite side.

Now I'm shaping the ear outline with a curved point sequence to make it bigger and more fox-like, verifying it doesn't self-intersect, then setting up the extrusion and shading with the orange coat color.

Still writing paint logic...

Then I'm defining the inner ear shape (a smaller pink flat shape offset forward from the base), and setting up the eye decals on the skull positioned using an azimuth angle to compute their x placement.

Now I'm scaling the skull from a sphere and thinking through how to add red vermilion kitsune-style markings on the shoulders and haunches using a conditional paint function based on position.

I decide decals are cleaner than paint logic: placing a red swirl flame-like SVG decal at the hip and shoulder, projected onto the body surface. I settle on using default up-axis orientation and not worrying too much about mirroring direction since it's largely arbitrary.

Adding haunch and shoulder muscle bulges...

Now I'm placing tail joints relative to the hips, setting each tail's base position and color, and planning the paint callbacks for each sweep so the atlas texel density stays reasonable across nine tails. I'm also working out the fan spread angles for the tail array using even increments.

Computing the actual curve coordinates for each tail segment, I'm checking that the total height with tails raised stays within a majestic but not excessive range, factoring in the flame addition on top, and adjusting the height falloff formula so the central tail doesn't push the silhouette too tall.

I'm also verifying that each tail starts from the same base point without visual clutter, and working through the joint naming scheme for the Catmull-Rom chain to avoid collisions like "tail1" vs "tail11" when indexing multiple tails and their control points.

Now I'm sketching a layered flame texture SVG with a purple outer teardrop shape, a cyan middle layer, and a white core, building the wavy flame silhouette path point by point.

Scaling the inner layers down and nesting them with translate/scale transforms so they center within the outer flame shape, then planning to parameterize the colors into a reusable flame-drawing function. Next I'm thinking through adding floating hitodama orb elements.

I'm computing orb positions spread across a 240-degree arc in front of the figure, keeping them clear of the tail, with varied heights to avoid any uniform floating look. No ground plane needed since this isn't a diorama, just floating elements with paws resting near y=0, and I'm double-checking leg foot targets stay grounded.

Checking front and hind leg segment lengths against root-to-foot distances to confirm the IK chains have enough slack for natural knee and hock bends rather than fully extending straight. The joint counts and parent attachments between spine, shoulders, and hips look consistent with how the limb and chain types are structured.

I'm figuring out how the body's spine chain should attach to the hips -- deciding whether to include the hips joint explicitly in the bone list so the tail-base region moves naturally with the spine rather than staying rigid, then sketching the rear-to-front path through the hips joint position.

Now I'm defining the body path points running from the rear through the hips and spine up toward the neck, along with the radii values at each cross-section, and considering making the body slightly narrower side-to-side than tall by scaling the x-radius relative to the y-radius for a more fox-like silhouette.

Next I'm laying out the neck as a two-segment chain continuing from the spine's end point up toward the head, tapering its radius from thicker at the base to narrower near the skull, and placing the head joint and skull center just past the neck's final point.

Still working out positions...

I'm now defining a wisp/tuft SVG shape as a simple curved teardrop path, and setting up the tail cards logic to scatter hit points along the tail sweep surface for rendering fur tufts.

Adding tail card scattering...

I'm thinking through the collar rope by taking a surface loop at the neck joint to build out that geometry.

Still writing collar details...

Adding the glowing gem offset above the pendant, then setting up tassel frame positions hanging below it for the dangling cards.

Each tassel card gets sized and flipped 180 degrees so it hangs downward, with an SVG showing a gold knot at the base and red strands flaring upward toward the attachment point. I'll skip the extra shimenawa details and just add a small gold earring accent on the ear.

Adding tail ring details...

For color, I'm setting tail tips to cream near the ends and orange elsewhere, using distance-based paint functions with closures over the tip point. Then I add flame-shaped cards at each tail tip sized for a glowing violet effect, with a second smaller flame layered per tail.

I'm skipping extra wisps along the body and reviewing my color palette—around a dozen flat colors like gold, red, ink, pink, cream, and orange plus gem tones, keeping in mind that cel paints don't add to that count. I'm also double-checking my imports to make sure I only pull in what's actually used: frame, rng, catmull, limb, paint, svg, and the toon exports like animeEye, cel, furEdge, INK, and glow, dropping anything unused like gradient or offset to avoid errors.

Now I'm setting up the module metadata with name, description, style tag "high-fantasy anime", and a commit hash, then writing the import statements and defining my color constants—orange, cream with a shadow tone, a dark sock purple, red, gold, and pink—before starting on the fur edge texture for the coat.

I'm figuring out how to render the leg socks with a clean transition zone using furEdge against the coat color, working through the right axis, teeth, and period values to get a convincing fur boundary at the right height on the leg.

For the head, I'm setting up a paint for the skull that blends orange into cream near the top using a positional furEdge, then reusing that same blend for the upper snout bridge so the muzzle color matches the skull, while giving the lower jaw its own plain cream paint.

Now I'm defining the ear paint and an animated eye with amber iris and pink blush, then sketching the facial markings as small SVG paths -- a crescent shape on the forehead with a center line, and curved streak marks on the cheek.

I'm also designing a flank swirl decal using a curved stroke path, scaling it up for crisp rendering, and preparing to apply it as a decal onto the body surface.

I'm placing the swirl decals symmetrically at the hips and shoulders on both sides of the body, letting the projection logic handle the x-offset near the surface, while skipping decals on the legs. I'm also planning ear details like a gold earring and a fur tuft.

Now I'm scattering wisp-shaped cards along the neck surface where the normal faces outward and downward, filtering hits by normal angle so they orient naturally along the tube's tilt, colored cream and angled for a flowing look. I'm skipping tail-base fluff but setting up a loop to generate multiple tail sweeps at varying angles around the body.

Still writing tail generation logic...

Adding a torus ring positioned along the tail's arc length at a chain point, oriented with a direction vector...

I'm scattering card hits across the tail surface for texture, adding white paint at the tail root, and collecting flame frames at the tail tip for a glow effect.

Now I'm adding small cream spike claws angled forward and slightly down on each paw.

I'm checking that spike tips still clear the ground, then setting up the leg joint chains—naming front limbs shoulder/elbow/wrist/paw and hind limbs hip/knee/hock/foot per side so each joint role stays unique and properly rooted under the hips.

Still writing haunch and shoulder geometry...
